semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The 'gp normative model' is a Gaussian Process-based approach to creating normative models, similar to the 'gamlss normative model'. Both aim to establish normative standards or responses in a probabilistic framework.

parent_models.justification: Both 'gamlss normative model' and 'gp normative model' fall under this as they describe models intended to define norms or standards.

closest_parent_model.justification: This category is broad enough to encompass both the 'gamlss normative model' and the 'gp normative model', making it the closest parent model.

child_models.justification: The 'gp normative model' is a specific application or version of the more general 'gamlss normative model', using Gaussian Processes.

closest_child_model.justification: As a Gaussian Process application of normative modeling, 'gp normative model' is the most directly derived and specific instance under 'gamlss normative model'.

sibling_models.justification: While not directly a normative model, it shares the statistical modeling approach with 'gamlss normative model'.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Shares the probabilistic and statistical approach characteristic of the 'gamlss normative model'.

unrelated_models.justification: There is no direct link between 'γ-model' and 'gamlss normative model' as the former is a completely different strategy.
